content.title: This Cruise Line Just Canceled All Winter Sailings to the Gulf—and It's Pivoting to a Gorgeous Caribbean Route
content.text: MSC World Europa has canceled its Arabian Gulf winter cruises and will now sail in the French Antilles. Published on April 9, 2026 Aerial view of MSC Poesia ship. Credit: MSC MSC Cruises has announced that MSC World Europa will no longer be sailing the Arabian Gulf this winter, joining Costa Cruises, AIDA Cruises, and Explora Journeys (owned by MSC) in canceling its upcoming schedule in the region. Originally set to sail from Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and Doha between November 2026 and April 2027, MSC World Europa is now being redeployed to the French Antilles, where it will depart on 7- and 14-night itineraries from Fort-de-France in Martinique, Pointe-à-Pitre in Guadeloupe, and Bridgetown in Barbados. “This adjustment offers guests a perfect winter-sun experience in one of the world’s most desirable warm-weather destinations, while offering all the innovative features and next-generation guest experiences for which MSC World Europa is known,” the company said in the announcement. The winter schedule was set to be MSC World Europa’s debut in the region; until now, the ship—which can accommodate nearly 7,000 passengers—has been based in the Mediterranean. Many of those affected are British and Europeans who were looking forward to a winter sun escape not too far from home. Those impacted were notified of the cancellation in an email from MSC, which has been shared on MSC World Europa Facebook groups. They have been given the option of transferring their booking to another MSC cruise of the same duration and cabin fare—with a guarantee to honor “the most favorable cruise fare between the original and the new booking”, the email stated. A variety of alternate sailings were suggested in the communication, including winter sun sailings onboard MSC Fantasia in Spain’s Canary Islands, Mediterranean cruises onboard several of its fleet, including its newest vessel, MSC World Asia, launching in December 2026, and Caribbean itineraries onboard ships including MSC World America—even rebooking on MSC World Europa in the French Antilles. The offer applies to the cruise fare only. “Flights and additional services are not included,” the email said. If none of the options are suitable, guests can request a full refund. Across social media, travelers have reported a variety of reactions, with higher airfares preventing many from considering joining the ship in the Caribbean. “We rebooked yesterday for Canaries cruise on the same dates,” said one Facebook user. Another on Reddit said they were considering transferring to MSC World Asia in Europe—but are hesitating because "it's probably not the best idea to travel the Mediterranean in winter." The shuffle means that cruisers in the Caribbean can now benefit from having two of MSC’s World-class vessels—MSC World Europa and MSC World America—to choose from in the region. MSC World Europa replaces MSC Seaview in the French Antilles this winter; that ship is now being redeployed to itineraries sailing to Brazil and Argentina. Related Stories
